title: Great skin on a small budget
teaser: Three cheap products do most of the work. Everything else is optional.

points.title: A gentle cleanser
points.detail: Any fragrance-free, low-foam wash. A pharmacy own-brand works as well as a premium one.

points.title: A plain moisturiser
points.detail: Look for glycerin, ceramides or petrolatum near the top of the list. A tub lasts months.

points.title: Sunscreen, SPF 30 or more
points.detail: The biggest anti-mark, anti-ageing step there is. Buy the one you will wear every day.

points.title: Petroleum jelly
points.detail: A thin layer over moisturiser at night seals in water. Ideal for dry, cracked or wind-burnt skin; skip it on breakout areas.

points.title: Generic actives
points.detail: Benzoyl peroxide 2.5–5%, salicylic acid 2% and adapalene 0.1% are the same molecules at any price.

points.title: Fewer products, used daily
points.detail: Two steps done every day beat ten done twice a week.

points.title: Pea-sized amounts
points.detail: A pea of cream covers the face; a dropper of serum is too much.

points.title: Keep it cool and closed
points.detail: Heat and light break down actives like vitamin C. Close lids tightly.

points.title: Scan your shelf first
points.detail: Before buying, check whether something you own already does the job.

title: Fruits and kitchen remedies: what helps, what burns
teaser: A few kitchen things soothe skin. Others cause burns and dark marks. Know which.

points.title: Oats for itchy, irritated skin
points.detail: Blend plain oats to a fine powder, stir into a lukewarm bath or mix with water to a paste. 10–15 minutes, rinse.

points.title: Raw honey as a mask
points.detail: A thin layer on clean skin for 10–15 minutes, rinse with lukewarm water. It holds moisture and is mildly antibacterial.

points.title: Fresh aloe vera gel
points.detail: Scoop the clear inner gel only (not the yellow sap), apply thinly after sun or irritation. Patch test first.

points.title: Cooled green tea compress
points.detail: Brew, chill, soak a clean cloth and hold it on red or puffy areas for 10 minutes.

points.title: Cold cucumber or spoons for puffy eyes
points.detail: The cold does the work, for an hour or so. Pleasant, not a treatment.

points.title: Lemon or lime juice
points.detail: Acid plus sun causes burns and blotchy dark marks that last months.

points.title: Baking soda and toothpaste
points.detail: Far too alkaline: they strip the barrier and leave redness worse than the spot.

points.title: Raw garlic, ginger, cinnamon
points.detail: They cause chemical burns on facial skin.

points.title: Sugar, salt or coffee scrubs
points.detail: Sharp grains tear the skin. Fine on rough feet, not on a face.

points.title: Undiluted vinegar
points.detail: Burns. Diluted, it still does nothing an actual product does better.

points.title: Coconut oil on acne-prone skin
points.detail: It clogs pores for many people. Keep it for body and hair.

points.title: Vitamin C fruit daily
points.detail: Guava, oranges, pawpaw, mango, pineapple, kiwi. Skin needs vitamin C to build collagen.

points.title: Tomatoes cooked with a little oil
points.detail: Lycopene gives a small boost to the skin's own sun defence. It never replaces sunscreen.

points.title: Avocado, groundnuts, seeds, oily fish
points.detail: Vitamin E and omega-3 fats support a comfortable, less inflamed barrier.

points.title: Watermelon, cucumber, oranges
points.detail: Mostly water: they count towards your daily water.

title: Skin-lightening creams: the hidden danger
teaser: Many "fairness" creams contain mercury or steroids. They damage skin for years.

points.title: Mercury
points.detail: Banned in cosmetics in most countries, still found in unlabelled creams. It poisons the kidneys and nerves.

points.title: Strong steroids (clobetasol, betamethasone)
points.detail: They thin skin, cause stretch marks, acne and permanent darkening when stopped.

points.title: High-strength hydroquinone without a doctor
points.detail: Long use can cause ochronosis: blue-black patches that are very hard to treat.

points.title: Fast, dramatic lightening
points.detail: Real mark-fading takes 8–12 weeks. Anything faster is usually a steroid.

points.title: No ingredient list or a vague one
points.detail: Unlabelled or "herbal secret formula" creams are the most likely to be contaminated.

points.title: Skin that gets worse when you stop
points.detail: Rebound darkening and spots after stopping are classic steroid withdrawal. See a doctor.

points.title: Daily sunscreen first
points.detail: Without it, nothing else works: sun re-darkens marks within hours.

points.title: Azelaic acid, niacinamide, vitamin C
points.detail: Gentle, proven mark-faders that are safe on deeper skin tones.

points.title: Treat the cause
points.detail: Fewer breakouts and no picking means fewer new marks.

title: Water and your skin
teaser: Enough water keeps skin from looking dull and tight. More than enough does nothing extra.

points.title: About 33 ml per kg of body weight
points.detail: Around 80% of that from drinks; food covers the rest. Your target is on Today.

points.title: More on hot days and when you sweat
points.detail: Add about half a litre per hour of exercise and on days over 30°C.

points.title: Pale yellow is the goal
points.detail: Dark urine means drink more; completely clear means you can ease off.

points.title: A glass with each routine
points.detail: Morning routine, glass. Evening routine, glass. Two done before you think about it.

points.title: Spread it out
points.detail: A glass every couple of hours beats a litre at night (and saves your sleep).

points.title: Tea, milk and fruit count
points.detail: Sugary drinks count as water but work against breakouts.

points.title: Water is not a moisturiser
points.detail: Dry, flaky skin needs a barrier cream. Drinking more won't fix it if you already drink enough.

title: Dress your skin for the weather
teaser: Heat, humidity, wind and sun each change what your skin needs. Adjust the routine, not just clothes.

points.title: Lighter moisturiser
points.detail: A gel or lotion instead of a thick cream; humidity already holds water in.

points.title: Rinse sweat quickly
points.detail: Within 30 minutes of sweating, especially under caps, helmets and straps.

points.title: Water-resistant sunscreen
points.detail: Reapply every two hours outside and after sweating.

points.title: Richer cream, sealed at night
points.detail: Low humidity pulls water out of skin. A thin layer of petroleum jelly over moisturiser helps.

points.title: Cleanse gently at night
points.detail: Dust and pollution sit on skin all day; one gentle cleanse removes them without stripping.

points.title: Fewer acids for a while
points.detail: Pause exfoliating acids if skin stings in dry wind.

points.title: UV 3 and above: sunscreen and shade
points.detail: Clouds block little UV. The UV index on Today tells you the day's peak.

points.title: Every skin tone needs it
points.detail: On deeper skin, UV darkens marks more than it burns.

points.title: Hats and shade count
points.detail: A wide brim cuts UV on the face by about half.

points.title: Lukewarm, not hot, water
points.detail: Hot showers on cold days strip the barrier fast.

points.title: Lip balm and a scarf
points.detail: Lips have no oil glands; wind cracks them first.

title: Pillows, sheets, towels and phones
teaser: Your skin spends hours pressed against fabric and screens. Keep them clean.

points.title: Pillowcase: every 2–3 nights if you break out
points.detail: Weekly otherwise. Flip it in between for a clean side.

points.title: Sheets: weekly
points.detail: Hot wash kills mites and bacteria; dry fully in sun or a dryer.

points.title: Face towel: your own, every 2–3 uses
points.detail: Pat, don't rub. A damp shared towel spreads bacteria.

points.title: Makeup brushes and sponges: weekly
points.detail: Mild soap, rinse, dry flat.

points.title: Wipe your phone daily
points.detail: It touches your cheek and jaw on every call. An alcohol wipe or a damp cloth with soap.

points.title: Hair oil and pomade off the forehead
points.detail: Oily hair products clog pores along the hairline. Wash your face after applying them.

points.title: Fragrance-free laundry if you're sensitive
points.detail: Fabric softener and scented detergent are common hidden irritants.

points.title: Satin or silk is optional
points.detail: Smoother on skin and hair, but a clean cotton case does the main job.

title: Eating for clearer skin
teaser: A few food patterns are linked to breakouts and redness. Test them on yourself for four weeks.

points.title: Sugary drinks and white carbs
points.detail: Fast-digesting sugar spikes hormones that drive oil. Swap soda and juice for water and whole grains.

points.title: Milk, especially skimmed
points.detail: Some people break out more on dairy. Try four weeks without and compare your scans.

points.title: Whey protein shakes
points.detail: A common trigger for jawline and back acne in gym-goers.

points.title: Alcohol, hot drinks, spicy food
points.detail: Classic flush triggers. Log them in check-ins to see which are yours.

points.title: Oily fish, beans, nuts and seeds
points.detail: Omega-3 fats and zinc calm inflammation.

points.title: Colourful fruit and vegetables
points.detail: Vitamin C and antioxidants help skin repair.

points.title: Chocolate, honestly
points.detail: The evidence is weak. If it's dark and low in sugar, don't worry about it.

points.title: One change at a time, four weeks
points.detail: Skin turns over in about a month. Change one thing, scan weekly, compare.

title: Sleep, stress and exercise
teaser: Stress hormones raise oil and slow repair. The basics show up in your scans.

points.title: 7–9 hours
points.detail: Skin repairs overnight; short sleep shows as dullness and dark circles.

points.title: Same side, clean case
points.detail: If breakouts sit on one cheek, it's often the side you sleep on.

points.title: Expect flares in stressful weeks
points.detail: Exams and deadlines raise cortisol and oil. Keep the routine simple then, don't add new actives.

points.title: Ten minutes a day
points.detail: A walk, breathing or prayer: anything that lowers stress shows up within weeks.

points.title: Sweat is fine, leaving it isn't
points.detail: Rinse or cleanse within 30 minutes and change out of damp clothes.

points.title: Sunscreen for outdoor training
points.detail: Water-resistant, reapplied every two hours.
